verdict.rationale: Ramp ships an official, open-source Ramp CLI (ramp-public/ramp-cli) that installs via script or Homebrew and authenticates with browser OAuth or a headless agent client-credentials login. It is built for agents: `--agent` gives JSON output, `--no-input` supports CI, there are profile switching and packaged skills, and 12 resources cover bills, cards, transactions, reimbursements and more. The AI Agents guide and llms.txt position it as the channel for coding agents and scripted workflows. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the CLI installs and runs as documented (the probe only confirms the repo location).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Authenticate with OAuth, manage expenses, approve bills, book travel, and more from your terminal or AI agent.
`--agent` outputs JSON for scripting and AI agent consumption
Standalone agents authenticate without a browser by exchanging OAuth client credentials for a production access token
The CLI outputs JSON in agent mode and is built for scripted loops
